Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming to iOS 27, the Passwords app is set to receive a particularly powerful capability: the ability to automatically change your passwords for you.

The Passwords app can fix compromised login details for you in iOS 27, powered by Apple Intelligence

A whole new era of Apple Intelligence is at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and its accompanying software updates. One powerful new AI feature relates directly to the Apple Passwords app.

When Passwords launched two years ago, it served as a dedicated centralised hub for login details, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

If any passwords in the database had issues, the app has always alerted you. For example, if your password was discovered in a data breach, or reused across multiple accounts, the Passwords app would let you know.

Until now, however, you've always had to fix these problematic login details manually yourself.

However, in iOS 27, Apple says that in many cases, its new agentic AI capabilities can change your passwords for you. According to its official website:

With this capability, you can ensure your login details remain secure and use sufficiently strong passwords at all times, while minimising the actions and time required.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and is expected to roll out to all users in the coming weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to debut with iOS 27.0, though its availability in the beta has been inconsistent, so it may be pushed back to iOS 27.1.

Have you tried the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How has your experience been? Let us know in the comments.
